description: Create a booking policy. Call get_booking_rules FIRST and reuse a matching set instead — these are shared company-wide, not per product. `weeklyHours` are LOCAL wall-clock times at the outlet; if neither the outlet nor the company has a timezone the engine refuses availability with a 400, so fix the outlet rather than guessing an offset. `bufferMinutes` consumes grid time for slot bookings (cleaning between appointments); for overnight stays use checkInTime/checkOutTime instead and leave the buffer at 0 — the cleaning window lives in the gap and does not consume a night.

bookingType.description: appointment = a person's time; rental = an asset; overnight = nights; group = a class

bufferMinutes.description: Dead time after each booking, e.g. 15 for cleaning. Consumes the grid

holdMinutes.description: How long an unpaid hold survives before the window frees itself. Default 10

maxAdvanceDays.description: How far ahead bookings open. 0 = no limit

name.description: How the merchant refers to it, e.g. "Haircuts 9–18"

ratePeriod.description: What ONE unit of price buys. `slot` for appointments and hourly rental. `week` and `month` are in the enum but NOT offered: the grid still cuts them one day at a time, so a weekly rate would be charged per day

slotLengthMinutes.description: How long one booking lasts, e.g. 30

weeklyHours.description: Opening hours per weekday, local time. Days left out are closed. For overnight stays leave hours off only if the property has none — an empty list there means every day.

name: hub_create_booking_rules
title: Create a booking rule set
